guided_journeys.story_title: The Institute Where Every Response Looked the Same
guided_journeys.tagline: Twelve dark nameplates, one stimulus-response tablet, and one rule. Identify the cue, responder, mechanism, experience, output, and consequence before the institute can separate one biological response from another.

guide.name: Dr. Mira Sen
guide.role: ecological-systems field curator who accompanies the learner through all eight Unit 8 journeys
guide.visual: dark field vest, waterproof notebook, a transparent ecology tablet that can display the current scale, organism or population identity, energy/matter arrows, and measured variables, plus a pointer used only to indicate real structures, graphs, reservoirs, or interactions
guide.story_job: Mira establishes the physical geography before terminology, keeps ecological scale and organism/population/community identity visible, changes one causal variable or transfer at a time, and names a term only after its defining pattern or mechanism can be reconstructed.

guided_journeys.premise: The Behavioral Response Institute has lost the distinctions among behavior, explanation level, learning, movement, communication, social fitness effects, and plant response. Dr. Mira Sen carries one transparent stimulus-response tablet through twelve fixed rooms. Each room can relight only after the visible biological mechanism separates the current concept from its nearest confusable alternative.
guided_journeys.mission: Travel the locked F2 route in order. Keep cue, responder, immediate mechanism, experience, behavioral output, and fitness or homeostasis consequence visible while separating proximate from ultimate explanation, innate from learned contribution, fixed response from trigger, migration from navigation cue, kinesis from taxis, signal from receiver response, imprinting from other learning, learning modes from one another, mating systems by relationship, altruism from cooperation, and phototaxis from phototropism.
guided_journeys.finale: The twelve room nameplates relight only after the learner can reconstruct each response from its cue and biological consequence. The route ends in the greenhouse with animal movement still distinct from directional plant growth and with behavioral explanations framed through mechanism, development, experience, survival, reproduction, and evolutionary history without intention or teleology.

guided_journeys.story_title: The Ledger That Would Not Balance
guided_journeys.tagline: Nine fixed stations, one two-column ledger, and one rule. Track where energy enters, where it becomes less available, and where matter remains conserved before the hall will let you leave.

guide.name: Dr. Mira Sen
guide.role: ecological-systems field curator who accompanies the learner through all eight Unit 8 journeys
guide.visual: dark field vest, waterproof notebook, a transparent ecology tablet that can display the current scale, organism or population identity, energy/matter arrows, and measured variables, plus a pointer used only to indicate real structures, graphs, reservoirs, or interactions
guide.story_job: Mira establishes the physical geography before terminology, keeps ecological scale and organism/population/community identity visible, changes one causal variable or transfer at a time, and names a term only after its defining pattern or mechanism can be reconstructed.

guided_journeys.premise: The Ecosystem Energy Exchange Hall has begun treating every ecological transfer as though energy and matter obeyed the same route. Dr. Mira Sen carries one transparent two-column ledger through nine fixed stations. The hall can balance only when organism budgets, thermoregulation, ecological scale, energy flow, matter cycling, carbon and energy acquisition, trophic roles, food-web direction, production, and trophic transfer remain causally distinct.
guided_journeys.mission: Travel the locked F2 route in order. Keep energy and matter in separate visible columns, preserve ecological scale, follow feeding arrows toward the receiving consumer, distinguish producer capture from respiration and heterotroph production, and treat trophic-transfer efficiency as variable rather than a universal ten-percent law.
guided_journeys.finale: The nine stations relight only after the learner can reconstruct energy input, transformation, respiration, heat dissipation, biomass production, feeding transfer, and matter conservation without recycling energy or losing track of reservoirs. The route ends with energy becoming progressively less available for biological work while matter remains traceable into the biogeochemical-cycle journey.

guided_journeys.story_title: The Watershed with the Missing Arrows
guided_journeys.tagline: Five fixed locations, four matter tracers, and one rule. Keep reservoirs stationary and move matter only when a real transfer process earns an arrow.

guide.name: Dr. Mira Sen
guide.role: ecological-systems field curator who accompanies the learner through all eight Unit 8 journeys
guide.visual: dark field vest, waterproof notebook, a transparent ecology tablet that can display the current scale, organism or population identity, energy/matter arrows, and measured variables, plus a pointer used only to indicate real structures, graphs, reservoirs, or interactions

guided_journeys.premise: The Biogeochemical Cycle Watershed has lost the arrows connecting its reservoirs. Dr. Mira Sen carries one transparent watershed reservoir board through five fixed locations. Each pathway returns only when the learner can distinguish where matter is stored from the process that moves it and can preserve the characteristic reservoirs and transformations of water, carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus.
guided_journeys.mission: Travel the locked F2 route in order. Keep reservoir boxes and transfer arrows physically distinct, follow the same matter through valid ecological processes, preserve the chemical direction of nitrogen transformations, and explain why the phosphorus cycle is primarily sedimentary without inventing a large atmospheric phosphorus reservoir.
guided_journeys.finale: The watershed map is restored after the learner can rebuild all four cycles from reservoirs and processes instead of memorized arrow shapes. Water, carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus share a reservoir-transfer grammar while retaining different dominant reservoirs, transformations, chemical directions, and timescales.

guided_journeys.story_title: The Reserve That Could Not Agree on One Population
guided_journeys.tagline: Seven fixed stations, one census identity, and one rule. Change the measurement without changing the population you are measuring.

guide.name: Dr. Mira Sen
guide.role: ecological-systems field curator who accompanies the learner through all eight Unit 8 journeys
guide.visual: dark field vest, waterproof notebook, a transparent ecology tablet that can display the current scale, organism or population identity, energy/matter arrows, and measured variables, plus a pointer used only to indicate real structures, graphs, reservoirs, or interactions
guide.story_job: Mira establishes the physical geography before terminology, keeps ecological scale and organism/population/community identity visible, changes one causal variable or transfer at a time, and names a term only after its defining pattern or mechanism can be reconstructed.

guided_journeys.premise: Population R17 keeps triggering apparently contradictory reserve reports because density, dispersion, age structure, survivorship, population change, and life-history strategy are being treated as if they were the same measurement. Dr. Mira Sen carries one census card through seven fixed stations so the learner can separate each quantity while keeping one population identity.
guided_journeys.mission: Travel the locked F2 route in order. Preserve population R17, its mapped boundary, cohort ledger, and N counter while changing only the measurement or comparison required at each station. Keep density separate from dispersion, life tables separate from survivorship curves, dN/dt separate from per-capita rate, and r/K language on a continuum rather than in rigid species boxes.
guided_journeys.finale: The reserve dashboard reconciles its reports after the learner reconstructs one population through seven different ecological questions. The same R17 population can have a density, a dispersion pattern, demographic structure, a survivorship pattern, an absolute population-change rate, life-history trade-offs, and context-dependent placement along the historical r/K continuum without those ideas becoming interchangeable.

guided_journeys.story_title: The Curve That Would Not Hold Still
guided_journeys.tagline: Five fixed control rooms, one population-growth dashboard, and one rule. Read the assumptions before trusting the curve.

guide.name: Dr. Mira Sen
guide.role: ecological-systems field curator who accompanies the learner through all eight Unit 8 journeys
guide.visual: dark field vest, waterproof notebook, a transparent ecology tablet that can display the current scale, organism or population identity, energy/matter arrows, and measured variables, plus a pointer used only to indicate real structures, graphs, reservoirs, or interactions

guided_journeys.premise: A population-growth control system keeps producing different curves and regulation labels from the same dashboard. Dr. Mira Sen carries N, time, rmax, K, per-capita effects, and graph axes through five rooms so each model or classification can be explained from its assumptions and mechanism.
guided_journeys.mission: Travel the locked F2 route in order. Keep one population-growth dashboard visible while moving from exponential growth to environment-dependent carrying capacity, logistic slowing, density-dependent regulation, and density-independent effects. Preserve dN/dt, rmax, N, and K as distinct quantities and diagnose regulation from per-capita effects rather than total counts.
guided_journeys.finale: The control center stabilizes after the learner reconstructs why a J curve follows exponential assumptions, why K moves with environmental conditions, why the logistic term slows growth as N approaches K, and why density dependence is diagnosed from how per-capita effects change with density.

guided_journeys.story_title: The District Where Every Relationship Left a Mark
guided_journeys.tagline: Eight fixed ecological stations, one shared community map, and one rule. Every relationship must leave a visible effect before it receives a name.

guide.name: Dr. Mira Sen
guide.role: ecological-systems field curator who accompanies the learner through all eight Unit 8 journeys
guide.visual: dark field vest, waterproof notebook, a transparent ecology tablet that can display the current scale, organism or population identity, energy/matter arrows, and measured variables, plus a pointer used only to indicate real structures, graphs, reservoirs, or interactions

guided_journeys.premise: A living district map keeps changing as species use habitat, overlap in niche, compete, consume, form close associations, and recover after disturbance. Dr. Mira Sen carries the same community map through eight locations so every label can be reconstructed from a visible ecological effect.
guided_journeys.mission: Travel the locked F2 route in order. Keep Species A, Species B, Species C, habitat layers, resource-use layers, abundance markers, and sign badges visible while separating habitat from niche, potential from realized niche, interaction effects from labels, competition from partitioning, consumer interactions from defenses, symbioses by sign, and succession by starting conditions.
guided_journeys.finale: The district becomes readable as one connected community system after the learner can explain why each map boundary, sign badge, abundance shift, resource-use band, disturbance mark, and succession path changed.
